stemMd: A student claims that Text 2 offers a physical explanation for why canopied streets lose their advantage overnight. Which quotation from Text 2 most effectively supports that claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: "dense canopy traps the heat that pavement releases at night"

options.label: B
options.textMd: "the city's heat-related hospital admissions cluster in the hours before dawn"

options.label: C
options.textMd: "does not dispute that tree-shaded streets are cooler at midday"

options.label: D
options.textMd: "his own overnight readings found no difference between canopied and treeless streets after 10 p.m."

explanationMd:
The claim has two parts, and the right quotation has to satisfy both: it must be an *explanation*, and it must be about the *overnight* loss of advantage.

Choice C is the only quotation that gives a physical cause. Pavement absorbs heat all day and releases it after dark; a dense canopy holds that released heat near the street instead of letting it escape upward. That is a mechanism, and it is specifically a nighttime one.

The trap here is choice B, which is about the same overnight period but reports the observation rather than explaining it. A useful test: ask whether the quotation answers "what happened?" or "why did it happen?" The claim asks for the second, and only C answers it.

distractorRationale.d: This is the finding the claim is trying to explain, not the explanation. It tells you that the advantage disappears after 10 p.m. but gives no reason; notice that the passage attaches "because" to a different clause.
distractorRationale.c: This is Lindqvist's concession about midday conditions. It establishes what he agrees with, and says nothing at all about night, so it cannot support a claim about overnight behaviour.
distractorRationale.b: This explains why the overnight result matters for public health, which is the reason Lindqvist cares about it. It is a point about consequences, not a physical account of why canopy stops helping.

accessibilityText: Choose the quotation from Text 2 that best supports the claim that Text 2 gives a physical explanation for why canopied streets lose their cooling advantage overnight.

provenance.notes: Original item; all quotations are taken from the original Text 2 written for this bank.

independentSolve.workingNotes: The claim asks for a physical explanation, and only 'dense canopy traps the heat that pavement releases at night' states a mechanism; B reports the observation being explained rather than the cause.
